opening_message:
Ticket 1: Nathaniel Young (employee ID E031) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E031.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Nathaniel Young (E031) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Request for write access to Payroll is within policy (full-time employees may have up to write; role owns the system). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E031 is a contractor with basic security training (note that prior note listed full-time — security record takes precedence). Contractors get read, or write only with advanced training. Since training is basic, maximum is read; requested write is above max. Recommend granting read.
reason: HR database (authoritative for employment type and role) shows E031 is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Under policy, full-time employees may have up to write access, and admin only if their role owns the system; Payroll Specialist owns Payroll. The requested write is at or below the maximum, so write is granted. The Security note's assertion that its record takes precedence is not backed by policy, and its employment type conflicts with HR's verified record; HR data is used for the decision.

- employment type: contractor (looked up)
- security training: basic (looked up)

1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

The conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor. The Security agent claims its record takes precedence (security record takes precedence over HR).

The key deciding factor: employment type. HR says full_time (looked up in own database). Security says contractor (looked up in own database). These conflict.
